title: FAA Part 107 loading, performance and safe operations practice questions
description: Free Part 107 practice questions on loading, performance, physiology, decision-making, radio and safe operations, each linked to its FAA source.

questions.question: According to the FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide, what determines where an aircraft's center of gravity (CG) is located?

options.A: A fixed point the manufacturer marks on the aircraft
options.B: The distribution of the aircraft's weight
options.C: The location of the center of pressure alone
options.D: The position of the control station antenna

questions.explanation: The Study Guide says "The CG is not a fixed point marked on the aircraft; its location depends on the distribution of aircraft weight."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.question: What does the Study Guide say will be necessary if the CG is not within the allowable limits after loading?

options.A: Flying at a higher airspeed to make up for it
options.B: Using steeper bank angles in turns
options.C: Climbing to a higher altitude before maneuvering
options.D: Relocating or shedding some weight before flight is attempted

questions.explanation: If the CG is not within the allowable limits, the Study Guide says "it will be necessary to relocate or shed some weight before flight is attempted."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.question: In what unit does the Study Guide say load factor is measured?

options.A: In Gs (acceleration of gravity)
options.B: In foot-pounds of kinetic energy
options.C: In knots of airspeed
options.D: In inches of mercury

questions.explanation: The Study Guide: "The load factor is measured in Gs (acceleration of gravity), a unit of force equal to the force exerted by gravity on a body at rest".

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.question: Besides high density altitude conditions, which factors does the Study Guide say to consider prior to takeoff because they may require a reduction in weight?

options.A: The aircraft's registration date and serial number
options.B: The number of satellites the control station receives
options.C: Runway/launch area length, surface, slope, surface wind, and the presence of obstacles
options.D: The frequency band used by the control link

questions.explanation: The Study Guide: "Other factors to consider prior to takeoff are runway/launch area length, surface, slope, surface wind, and the presence of obstacles. These factors may require a reduction in weight prior to flight."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.question: According to the Study Guide, during a coordinated turn at a constant altitude, which two forces result in the load factor?

options.A: Lift and drag
options.B: Thrust and drag
options.C: Centrifugal force and weight
options.D: Thrust and lift

questions.explanation: The Study Guide: "At a constant altitude, during a coordinated turn in any aircraft, the load factor is the result of two forces: centrifugal force and weight."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.question: In the atmosphere both temperature and pressure decrease with altitude. According to the Study Guide, why can pilots still expect air density to decrease with altitude?

options.A: The fairly rapid drop in pressure as altitude is increased usually has the dominant effect
options.B: Temperature rises with altitude and lowers the density
options.C: Humidity always increases with altitude
options.D: Pressure has no effect on air density

questions.explanation: The Study Guide: "the fairly rapid drop in pressure as altitude is increased usually has the dominant effect. Hence, pilots can expect the density to decrease with altitude."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.question: What does the Study Guide advise when manufacturer-published performance data for a small UA is unavailable?

options.A: Flying without regard to performance limits
options.B: Asking air traffic control for the aircraft's performance data
options.C: Using data from any aircraft of similar weight
options.D: Seeking out performance data published by other users of the same small UA manufacturer model as a starting point

questions.explanation: The Study Guide says "it is advisable to seek out performance data that may have already been determined and published by other users of the same small UA manufacturer model and use that data as a starting point."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.question: When does 107.15(b) prohibit continuing the flight of the small unmanned aircraft?

options.A: When the battery charge falls below half
options.B: When he or she knows or has reason to know that the small unmanned aircraft system is no longer in a condition for safe operation
options.C: When the flight has lasted more than 30 minutes
options.D: When a light breeze begins to blow

questions.explanation: 107.15(b): "No person may continue flight of the small unmanned aircraft when he or she knows or has reason to know that the small unmanned aircraft system is no longer in a condition for safe operation."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 107.15, Condition for safe operation (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: According to the Study Guide, how are the features of an automated UNICOM system typically selected?

options.A: By microphone clicks on the UNICOM frequency
options.B: By a telephone call to Flight Service
options.C: By a text message to the airport manager
options.D: By entering a code in the Remote ID broadcast

questions.explanation: The Study Guide says automated UNICOM systems "offer a variety of features, typically selectable by microphone clicks, on the UNICOM frequency."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.question: Which item does 107.49(c) require the remote pilot in command to ensure prior to flight?

options.A: That the control station is at least 400 feet from any road
options.B: That the aircraft's firmware is the newest version released
options.C: That the flight has been announced on the CTAF
options.D: That all control links between ground control station and the small unmanned aircraft are working properly

questions.explanation: Prior to flight, the remote pilot in command must, under 107.49(c), "Ensure that all control links between ground control station and the small unmanned aircraft are working properly".

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 107.49, Preflight familiarization, inspection, and actions for aircraft operation (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What does 107.49(e) require the remote pilot in command to ensure, prior to flight, about any object attached or carried by the small unmanned aircraft?

options.A: That it weighs less than 5 pounds
options.B: That it is secure and does not adversely affect the flight characteristics or controllability of the aircraft
options.C: That it is registered separately with the FAA
options.D: That it is painted a high-visibility color

questions.explanation: 107.49(e): "Ensure that any object attached or carried by the small unmanned aircraft is secure and does not adversely affect the flight characteristics or controllability of the aircraft".

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 107.49, Preflight familiarization, inspection, and actions for aircraft operation (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Which persons does 107.17 cover when it bars someone who knows or has reason to know of a physical or mental condition that would interfere with safe operation of the small UAS?

options.A: Only the remote pilot in command
options.B: Only a person who holds a part 61 pilot certificate
options.C: A person manipulating the flight controls, or acting as a remote pilot in command, visual observer, or direct participant in the operation
options.D: Only the visual observer, if one is used

questions.explanation: 107.17: "No person may manipulate the flight controls of a small unmanned aircraft system or act as a remote pilot in command, visual observer, or direct participant in the operation of the small unmanned aircraft" if he or she knows or has reason to know of such a condition.

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 107.17, Medical condition (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Which kind of over-the-counter medication does the Study Guide name as an example that may cause drowsiness?

options.A: Vitamin supplements
options.B: Antibiotics
options.C: Sunscreen lotions
options.D: Certain antihistamines and decongestants

questions.explanation: The Study Guide notes that certain over-the-counter medications could affect the ability to safely operate a small UA: "For example, certain antihistamines and decongestants may cause drowsiness."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.question: Besides the medication questions of IMSAFE, which item does the Study Guide list for pilots to also consider?

options.A: Ensure adequate sleep the night prior to the flight
options.B: Skip meals on the day of the flight to stay alert
options.C: Limit water so that fewer breaks are needed
options.D: Take an elective medication the morning of the flight

questions.explanation: The Study Guide: "In addition to medication questions, pilots should also consider the following", including "Ensure adequate sleep the night prior to the flight", "Make sure you eat regular balanced meals" and "Do not take any unnecessary or elective medications."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.question: Which diuretic drinks does the Study Guide name among the causes of dehydration?

options.A: Plain water and sport drinks
options.B: Coffee, tea, alcohol, and caffeinated soft drinks
options.C: Milk and fruit juice
options.D: Energy drinks only

questions.explanation: The Study Guide: "Causes of dehydration are hot temperatures, wind, humidity, and diuretic drinks—coffee, tea, alcohol, and caffeinated soft drinks."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.question: According to the Study Guide, what is both the best prevention and the best cure for hyperventilation?

options.A: Drinking a caffeinated soft drink
options.B: Increasing the breathing rate
options.C: Breathing normally
options.D: Taking an antihistamine

questions.explanation: The Study Guide says "Breathing normally is both the best prevention and the best cure for hyperventilation."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.question: How does the Study Guide define heatstroke?

options.A: A condition caused by any inability of the body to control its temperature
options.B: An excessive rate and depth of respiration leading to abnormal loss of carbon dioxide
options.C: Short-term tiredness after strenuous effort or lack of sleep
options.D: The body's response to physical and psychological demands

questions.explanation: The Study Guide: "Heatstroke is a condition caused by any inability of the body to control its temperature."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.question: According to the Study Guide, why should antidotes be memorized for each of the hazardous attitudes?

options.A: So they can be read back to air traffic control
options.B: So the visual observer can check them before each flight
options.C: So they replace the preflight assessment of the operating environment
options.D: So they automatically come to mind when needed

questions.explanation: The Study Guide: after recognizing a thought as hazardous, "the pilot should label it as hazardous, then state the corresponding antidote. Antidotes should be memorized for each of the hazardous attitudes so they automatically come to mind when needed."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.question: In the Study Guide's 3P model, what does the TEAM choice list used to perform risk management stand for?

options.A: Test, Evaluate, Act, Monitor
options.B: Time, Environment, Aircraft, Mission
options.C: Transfer, Eliminate, Accept, or Mitigate
options.D: Task, Equipment, Airspace, Maintenance

questions.explanation: The Study Guide says pilots "can perform risk management by using the TEAM choice list of: Transfer, Eliminate, Accept, or Mitigate."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.question: According to the Study Guide, what are the three ways for pilots to communicate their intention and obtain airport/traffic information at an airport that does not have an operating tower?

options.A: By telephone, e-mail, or text message to the airport manager
options.B: By communicating with an FSS, a UNICOM operator, or by making a self-announce broadcast
options.C: By ADS-B Out, a transponder, or a Remote ID broadcast
options.D: Only by calling the nearest approach control

questions.explanation: The Study Guide names three ways at an airport without an operating tower: "by communicating with an FSS, a UNICOM operator, or by making a self-announce broadcast."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)
